### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via registerAuthzMiddleware (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `87eb4d4dab94e0cf93b8ca9d3104a0e5c5800fc8` — the merge of head `8383be875be9fd0fb9c04b7c388c504b72629538` into base `767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 87eb4d4dab94e0cf93b8ca9d3104a0e5c5800fc8 && git checkout 87eb4d4dab94e0cf93b8ca9d3104a0e5c5800fc8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb 8383be875be9fd0fb9c04b7c388c504b72629538 && git checkout -B drift-repro 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb && git merge --no-ff 8383be875be9fd0fb9c04b7c388c504b72629538

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 767f110690c680865b33400f221a03defeda52fb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8383be875be9fd0fb9c04b7c388c504b72629538`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts

Rendered 2026-11-11T08:26Z by a contract-review subagent. Inputs: card #32341 (body, triage comment, claim comment), PR #32403 (body, the 5-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge-base `aab20c10d7`), and the check-runs on the head (56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed). The remainder of the diff (the two test files and the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not judged in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New catalog key `record_queue_assign_denied` in `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES`: not a Clause-② widening. `Clause-②: no` is right.**
  - The exported const keeps its declared type, `Record` of string to `Record` of string to string. No exported key union or key type exists for this catalog. The one union that names the keys, `UserFacingDenialKey` in the middleware, is module-private. The spec `api-surface` and `export-origins` snapshots list the const by name and are untouched by the diff.
  - No schema, accept set, door request or door response changes shape. The catalog key is never on the wire: `withUserMessage` attaches the rendered string only, and the body `mapDataError` emits keeps the members `code`, `error`, `object`, `userMessage`.
  - What does grow is one override address, `errors.record_queue_assign_denied`, that a deployment `translation` item can now define with effect. That is the weakest sense of surface. The changeset names it, and the catalog's earlier key additions were read the same way. Had the line read `yes (widening)`, the level and this review would be the same.
- **The create refusal's `userMessage` text changes: right, and it narrows nothing released.** The sentence it replaces on the create, `record_queue_change_denied`, has not shipped: no `packages/**/CHANGELOG.md` names the key, and its introducing changeset (`.changeset/32278-security-403-user-message.md`) is still pending on `main`. Both queue keys reach their first release together, so no deployed override of the change key loses coverage of the create.
- **`denyQueueWrite` gains a required second parameter: right.** It is a closure local to the ownership step with exactly two call sites, both in the diff. Nothing public.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No authorable key, accepted value or default moves; the `Spec property liveness` and `Check Changeset` runs are green on the head.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `patch`. Those are the two packages whose `src/**` the diff moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` ships `patch` whatever the arm (Post-Task Checklist 3), so the level is right.
- Both declaration lines are present and line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and they agree: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- Observation, ungraded (changesets are outside ④): the changeset describes a correction to a sentence that never shipped. In the published `CHANGELOG.md` it will sit beside #32278's entry in the same release, which makes it readable.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The card's fork (one sentence for both verbs, or a separate create key) was left to the dev. The dev took the separate key. Answered: right, see ④. The two sites do not share a next step, so one sentence would be wrong on one of them.
- Dev flag: two derived gates were NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`). Answered by the head's check-runs: `Build Core`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are all success.
- Dev flag: `labelList` (#32342) untouched. Confirmed, the diff has no hunk near it.
- The docs-drift bot named `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` through the `registerAuthzMiddleware` symbol. That page says nothing about the queue refusal or its `userMessage`. No docs change is owed.
- The card, the claim and the PR body carry no `open_questions` entry. Nothing is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` (hits).** Read against the ownership step in the middleware and the admission table in `ownership-queue-gate.ts`.

- Key-table row for `record_queue_assign_denied`, "create a record in a queue they do not belong to; leave the queue blank or choose one they belong to". Holds. The insert branch refuses only when a queue is supplied, the caller lacks the transfer grant and `isMember` is false. Both remedies are admitted by the same branch: an absent, `null` or empty `queue` is not a supplied queue, and a member's insert passes.
- Reworded row for `record_queue_change_denied`, "change which queue an existing record is in (put it in one, take it out, or move it to another)". Holds. On update, without the grant, every written `queue` that is not an echo of the stored value is refused, which covers null to name, name to null and name to name.
- jsdoc, "a change of an existing record's queue is admitted for no member". Holds. The update branch never consults membership for a queue change; only `hasTransferGrant()` admits one.
- jsdoc, "the five ownership and queue keys take no placeholders". Holds: three owner keys and two queue keys, none with a placeholder in any locale.
- Locales. All four bundles (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`) carry the new key, and each bundle now holds the same 16 keys. The `zh-CN` sentence uses the full-width comma and period (#12717). No sentence names a grant, an API name or `owner_id`. The four translations say the same thing as the `en` sentence.
- Disclosure. The new sentence tells the caller they are not in the queue they named. The developer `message` on the same response already says so, and an unresolvable queue already answers `QUEUE_NOT_FOUND`, so the sentence opens no new oracle.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` (implementing).**

- The insert site passes `record_queue_assign_denied`, and the update site passes `record_queue_change_denied`. These are the only two `denyQueueWrite` call sites in the tree. The code agrees with both table rows.
- Status, `code`, `message`, `details`. Unchanged on both paths. The `PermissionDeniedError` is built from the same template, the same `INSERT_QUEUE_REFUSAL` / `MOVE_REFUSAL` constant and the same `refusalDetails` object as on `main`. The diff changes one thing in the closure: the key handed to `userFacingDenialMessage`. On the update path that key is the one `main` hard-coded, so the update refusal is identical in every member, `userMessage` included.
- The step comment listing the situations now names the create into a queue apart from the change. It agrees with the code.
- Attempts to break it:
  - A guest's queue write throws before either site and carries no `userMessage`, as on `main`.
  - With no queue service registered, `assertQueueResolves` throws `QUEUE_NOT_FOUND` before the insert site, so the new sentence is never rendered for a queue that does not resolve.
  - A bulk or invisible-row update has no pre-image and fails closed with the change key, which fits "an existing record".
  - A deployment override resolves under `errors.record_queue_assign_denied` ahead of the built-in bundle, through the unchanged `renderOperationMessage` ladder.

Findings:

- **nit** — `operation-message.ts`, module header: "`PERMISSION_DENIED` now carries three" (keys) sits above a table that lists ten `PERMISSION_DENIED` keys after this diff. The sentence predates this PR and was already stale after #32278; this diff adds one more row under it. No effect on correctness or the contract. Left as an accepted deviation, or a follow-up card.
- **nit** — the `en` sentence reads "create a record in that queue" on a batch insert too, where several rows may name queues. The sibling `record_owner_assign_denied` has the same singular shape. Accepted deviation.

No must-fix. No should-fix. Nits alone end the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32341-queue-denied-create-copy`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w` (contract-review subagent)

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ACCEPT addendum: the `protocol:system` label · 2026-11-11T08:30Z

The labeler added `protocol:system` because of the path: the diff touches `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`. Under the spec lane's fallback rule, a product-lane PR labelled `protocol:*` stops and its protocol hunk moves to a spec child. I read that rule and judged it does not apply here:
- The hunk is one key in the user-facing operation-message catalog, in four locales, plus its table row. That is error guidance prose, which the spec lane names as a piggyback item (`lanes/spec.md`: "含 describe/JSDoc、墓碑散文、错误 guidance").
- It is not authorable metadata: no schema shape, accepted value or default moves (`Metadata-protocol: none`). The at-tier record 6790975429 reviewed it as a hits file.

There is no protocol hunk to move, so the landing stands.
